body:
## Assessment scope and upstream basis

Skill: design-review. This independent rereview covers the complete revised package: review-closeout at docs/design/review-closeout/review-closeout.md and workflow at docs/design/workflow/workflow.md, bound by structured subjects. Both members were read in full, including the Design-owned clause map, revised policy references, and user-requested combined-condition judgment policy. The upstream record is proposal-review in this root, on proposal sha256:bbb68e34c2215a88c62e26c74d532520d030a97d2083e95e7605ad3f9f6736b9. The accepted direction remains applicable: the revisions implement its single-owner and explicit-judgment goals without changing its scope. The ordered overlap rule is an explicitly requested Design refinement, not unapproved authority inferred from storage.

Record Format remains the stored-representation dependency; no changed schema or mechanical interface is required by these corrections. Workflow's explicit domain indirection resolves retained dependency descriptions to RC assessment ownership without adding a second policy owner. The selected model convention combines requirements, architecture and decisions; no separate ADR is applicable.

## Package assessment

Architecture support: pass. Specialist assessment scopes, explicit current reliance, correction ownership, mandatory fresh whole-change Code Review and success-only Verify form a coherent realization of the proposal. Record-level applicability and existing narrative/subject structures carry scope distinctions without new fields or commands.

Proposal preservation and ownership: pass. The clause-level map now assigns identified source obligations to RC, retained specialist methods, historical contracts or storage/coordination dependencies. It distinguishes v3 freshness labels and proof layouts from current substantive reuse conditions, clean-with-notes/mixed-evidence historical rules from adopted judgment precedence, and specialist finding criteria from overall judgment. Newly discovered policy clauses explicitly return to Design; Delivery receives allocation and implementation work rather than authority to choose ownership. The map plus retained WF-ID mappings is sufficient to plan the bounded extraction while requiring complete transitive consumer reconciliation before adoption.

Cross-model consistency: pass. Workflow's actor table and primary interaction paragraphs reference RC for restrictions/restoration, rereview, sufficient inspection, multi-check reliance and concern disposition. RF/CLI references retain addressing, granularity, immutable origin and persistence. RC-SR-06 and RC-SR-15 preserve conservative restriction and individual-result inspection, so deleting the old Workflow formulations loses no inspected obligation. Runtime examples are identified as applications of the owning rules.

Judgment coherence: pass. The ordered rule distinguishes necessary authority decisions, material incompleteness of required scope, actionable defects and satisfied criteria. Concrete supported findings survive blocked or inconclusive outcomes. The rule prevents scope narrowing to manufacture approval, keeps unrelated decisions outside the test and treats optional improvements as advisory. Examples cover overlapping defects/decisions, partial evidence with a bounded defect and optional notes. Historical precedence remains explicitly contract-scoped. This is a deliberate semantic choice with adequate boundaries, not a CLI readiness algorithm.

Failure, recovery and compatibility: pass. Revised engineering work triggers appropriate independent reassessment; storage-only revisions do not automatically invalidate judgment; contradictory new proof still prevents unjustified reliance. Reporter-owned disposition and Verify-owned blockers survive later approval. Final-review correction and triggered CI changes require renewed integrated assessment. Historical subjects, procedures and origin guarantees remain scoped, and activation/publication require their separate authority.

Delivery sufficiency: pass. Stable RC/WF requirements, eight boundary dimensions and selected composed hazards provide allocation targets. Concrete file edits, packaged factoring, verification groups and execution evidence remain Delivery work. No implementation or installed-package proof is claimed at this Design gate.

## Correction disposition basis

The separate structured resolutions preserve each finding's original evidence, required outcome and immutable origin. Disposition is based on this reviewer's direct semantic inspection of the changed package; the cited design-draft-structure evidence supports only structural/readability currency. Complete-package assessment was repeated rather than treating finding-only fixes as sufficient approval.

Current context's subject-drift observations correspond to the retained old review/finding basis before rereview. Those identities are historical evidence and are not rewritten into the new engineering subjects. The current judgment binds the revised package; resolution rationales identify why the original concerns no longer require correction.

## Evidence and boundary coverage

All eight dimensions remain applicable: inputs/overlapping judgments, lifecycle/final checkpoint, identity/authority, composed specialist/consumer paths, temporal applicability/retry, failure/correction, historical compatibility and portable external environments. Material combined hazards include incomplete scope with actionable findings, owner decisions with defects, integrated correction after final review, new failed evidence without an engineering edit, concurrent model changes, Verify-owned blockers and single-milestone checkpoint omission. Their outcomes are requirement-owned and examples add no independent policy.

Inspected basis includes current proposal and upstream review, Constitution/Vision, complete package, retained Record Format boundaries, canonical Code Review/plan/Verify methods, Delivery Review allocation criteria, v3 evidence-applicability and successful-explanation references. No-map rationale: named canonical policy subjects supply the bounded assessment basis without repository-map state inference.

Validation run: python scripts/validate-boundary-first.py --check --path docs/design/review-closeout/review-closeout.md --path docs/design/workflow/workflow.md. Passed, structure-and-references-only. Existing exact-subject design-draft-structure evidence was inspected, including its actual commands and limited author claim. CLI subject inspection supplied the declared reads and exact identities for this save.

## Recording and isolation

This is a direct isolated Design rereview under rigorloop-records-v2. The stable review and explicit finding dispositions are recorded through primary batch, preserving origin; no historical round receipt, migration or package-settlement command is used. The judgment establishes an adequate exact Design basis for authorized Delivery planning only. It does not execute that stage or authorize implementation, activation, release, PR creation or final completion. No model, proposal or routing edit was made by this reviewer.

findings.evidence: Severity: major. Finding scope: artifact-local. Affected artifact IDs: review-closeout. Owning stages: design. Location: docs/design/review-closeout/review-closeout.md:122-148 (Consumer ownership and adoption inventory; Historical applicability and adoption). The accepted proposal at docs/proposals/2026-09-07-unify-review-closeout-policy.md:79 assigns Design the mapping of each affected current rule to its retained or replacement owner and distinction of historical behavior. The draft maps whole skills/reference families to wide RC ranges and says Delivery must enumerate affected clauses. For example, the Verify family includes v3 evidence-applicability freshness overrides/proof-shape obligations while RC-SR-15 defines general evidence reuse; the inventory does not identify which individual rules remain historically scoped, stay specialist-owned, or become RC-owned. This postpones policy ownership decisions, beyond ordinary file/check allocation.

origin.rationale: The change is justified by preventing existing obligations from being lost across policy and consumers. Broad family coverage cannot show that each obligation is retained or assigned, and transferring that semantic work to Delivery weakens the accepted Design boundary.
origin.required_outcome: Complete a Design-owned clause-level ownership and contract-scope map for affected shared rules and explicitly retained specialist rules, with exact source clause/ID or section and retained/replacement owner. Safe resolution path: design author expands/reconciles the map in review-closeout, preserving all proposal obligations; return the exact two-model package to independent Design Review. No upstream direction decision is needed.

resolution.rationale: The corrected review-closeout Clause-level policy ownership decisions table identifies concrete source clauses and separates current shared obligations, retained specialist criteria, historical-only protocols and dependencies. Design retains ownership of further unmapped clauses. Delivery now implements settled decisions rather than choosing semantic ownership. I independently inspected the complete revised package and relevant source clauses; the original required outcome is satisfied.

findings.evidence: Severity: major. Finding scope: cross-artifact. Affected artifact IDs: workflow, review-closeout. Owning stages: design. Location: docs/design/workflow/workflow.md:158,180-182 (Responsibility-specific updates; Primary skill interaction and decision ownership), and docs/design/review-closeout/review-closeout.md RC-SR-05/06/07/16/17 and RC-DEC-01. Workflow still independently states who can restrict/restore evidence, requires actual independent rereview before replacing an assessment, requires authors to declare impact, and defines evidence-restriction/reliance duties. These are substantive assessment rules in the Building Block View, not the Runtime illustrations described by the extraction note. RC now defines the same applicability/reassessment duties, while its ownership contract says Workflow must reference rather than define them again. Some paragraphs also combine these duplicates with legitimate Record Format/CLI mechanics, obscuring which owner governs a future correction.

resolution.rationale: The revised Workflow Responsibility-specific updates and Primary skill interaction sections replace the cited independent rules with RC-SR-02/05–10/15/18 references. Record granularity, construction and origin mechanics point to RF/CLI. RC-SR-06 explicitly retains conservative restrictions and assessor-only restoration; RC-SR-15 retains restriction and individual-result assessment for multi-check records. The actor table is expressly an assignment index and runtime passages are policy applications. independence_basis: The separate delegated reviewer did not author or edit either model or their corrections. The user supplied additional judgment-policy intent and codex-root authored the engineering revisions. This reviewer previously recorded independent findings, then read both revised members in full and assessed corrections and complete coherence separately. A distinct reviewing execution with no engineering authorship establishes independence; role labels and passed validators alone do not.
